osmTags.inscription: Abergavenny was known for its flannel, a fine soft woollen cloth. Here was the site of a flannel mill in the 18th century.
Sheep market on this site until 1863
Site of Roman barracks and granary, also line of the 1241 Norman town wall
Near this spot stood the south east gate of the Roman fort of Gobannium
Site of the medieval west gate
Thanks to pupils of Gilwern Primary School for assisting with the research and the 18 anonymous medieval artists and tile makers for creating the original images. Ceramic by Ned Heywood
Here stood the Bull Inn alongside the town's medieval market place

eras.label: Mapped site · auto T1
eras.summary: Mapped outline, terrain and present-day surroundings from open data. No historic reconstruction.
eras.basis: Everything drawn is traced from OpenStreetMap ways (ODbL) and the Terrarium elevation tiles. Each element names its OSM way.
eras.conjecture: Walls and buildings without a sourced height are drawn as kerb-high plan lines, never as masses. Closed walls have no gates: none are mapped. The DEM is ~30 m source resolution: it cannot show terraces, ditches or scarps. Nothing historic is depicted.
